## **Loading data***
```{r}
remove(list = ls())
library(tidyverse)
library(asreml)
library(mvngGrAd)
library(SpATS)
library(kableExtra)
library(patchwork)

load('mydata.Rdata')
source('SpatialAnalysisFun.R')

df.ty = mydata %>% 
  filter(year_trial == '2026_I4' & trait == 'TY') %>%   
  droplevels() %>%
  select(row, col, check, rep, clone, trait, value) %>%
  arrange(row, col)
```

## **Model 1:** Baseline
$$
y_{ijk} = \mu + C_k+B_j+G_i+e_{ijk}
$$

- $\mu$ Overal mean

- $C_k$ Vector of fixed checks effects

- $R_j$ Vector of fixed blocks effects

- $G_i$ Vector of random genotypes effects, $\sim N(0, I\sigma_g^2)$

- $e_{ijk}$ Vector of random residual effects, $\sim N(0, I\sigma_{e}^2)$

**Testing significance of random effect (Genotypes)**

As we want to verify the difference between the genotypes. And `clone` was modeled as random effects, by simple testing:

- $H_0:\sigma_g = 0$

- $H_a:\sigma_g \neq 0$

We can verify if there is variability between them by performing an ANOVA or Mixed Models.

### ANOVA

$$
y_{ijk} = \mu +B_j+G_i+e_{ijk}
$$

$$
y_{ijk} = \mu +C_k+B_j+G_i+e_{ijk}
$$

Where:

- $C_k$ is effects of checks - if included

- $B_j$ is the effects of Blocks

- $G_i$ is the effects of genotypes

- $e_{ijk}$ is the residual

```{r}
M1_A.ty = lm(value~rep+clone, data = df.ty)
anova(M1_A.ty)

M1_A2.ty = lm(value~check+rep+clone,data = df.ty)
anova(M1_A2.ty)
```

When ANOVA was performed with and without including checks as a factor, the only significant differences were observed among block levels. And genotypes did not differ significantly in their means, as indicated by the F-test (P > 0.05).

### Mixed Models
```{r}
# --- Total Yield (TY)
M1.ty = asreml(value ~ 1+check+rep,
               random = ~clone,
               na.action = na.method(x = "include"),
               data = df.ty)

plot(M1.ty)

vc.M1 = summary(M1.ty)$varcomp;vc.M1

AIC[1] = as.numeric(summary(M1.ty)$aic[1])
BIC[1] = as.numeric(summary(M1.ty)$bic[1])
H2[1] = as.numeric(vpredict(M1.ty, H2~V1/(V1+V2))[1])
varG[1] = as.numeric(vc.M1[1,1])
varE[1] = as.numeric(vc.M1[2,1])

M1r.ty = asreml(value ~ 1+check+rep,
                na.action = na.method(x = "include"),
                data = df.ty)

lrt(M1.ty, M1r.ty, boundary = T)
```

Mixed Model 1 also showed no significant differences among clones for Total Yield, based on the likelihood ratio test (LRT) comparing the complete model with and without the random clone effect.

```{r}
df.ty %>% group_by(clone) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(mean = mean(value)) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean))
```

## **Model 2:** (AR1 x AR1) 

Modeling autoregressive correlation of residuals (AR1 x AR1)

$$
y_{ijk} = \mu+C_k+B_j+G_i+e_{ijk}
$$

- $e_{ijk}$ Vector of random residual effects, $\sim N(0, \sigma_e\Sigma_r(\rho_r)\otimes\Sigma_c(\rho_c))$

```{r}
# --- TY
M2.ty = asreml(value ~ 1+check+rep,
               random = ~ clone,
               na.action = na.method(x = 'include'),
               residual = ~ar1(row):ar1(col),
               data = df.ty)

plot(M2.ty)

vc.M2 = summary(M2.ty)$varcomp;vc.M2

AIC[2] = as.numeric(summary(M2.ty)$aic[1])
BIC[2] = as.numeric(summary(M2.ty)$bic[1])
H2[2] = as.numeric(vpredict(M2.ty, H2~V1/(V1+V2))[1])
varG[2] = as.numeric(vc.M2[1,1])
varE[2] = as.numeric(vc.M2[2,1])

M2r.ty = asreml(value ~ 1+check+rep,
                na.action = na.method(x = 'include'),
                residual = ~ar1(row):ar1(col),
                data = df.ty)

lrt(M2.ty, M2r.ty)

plot(varioGram(M2.ty))
```
Now, the genotype random term has variability within its levels. 

## **Model 3:** AR1, with fixed column
$$
y_{ijkl} = \mu +C_k+B_j+COL_l+G_i+e_{ijkl}
$$

- $\mu$ Overal mean

- $C_k$ Vector of fixed checks effects

- $B_j$ Vector of fixed blocks effects

- $COL_l$ Vector of fixed collumns effects

- $G_i$ Vector of random genotypes effects, $\sim N(0, I\sigma_g^2)$

- $e_{ijkl}$ Vector of random residual effects, $\sim N(0, \Sigma_r(\rho_r)\otimes\Sigma_c(\rho_c))$

```{r}
df.ty$Fcol = factor(as.numeric(df.ty$col))

# --- TY
M3.ty = asreml(value ~ 1+check+rep+Fcol,
               random = ~clone,
               na.action = na.method(x = "include"),
               residual = ~ar1(row):ar1(col),
               data = df.ty)
plot(M3.ty)
vc.M3 = summary(M3.ty)$varcomp; vc.M3

AIC[3] = as.numeric(summary(M3.ty)$aic[1])
BIC[3] = as.numeric(summary(M3.ty)$bic[1])
H2[3] = as.numeric(vpredict(M3.ty, H2~V1/(V1+V2))[1])
varG[3] = as.numeric(vc.M3[1,1])
varE[3] = as.numeric(vc.M3[2,1])

M3r.ty = asreml(value ~ 1+check+rep+Fcol,
                na.action = na.method(x = "include"),
                residual = ~ar1(row):ar1(col),
                data = df.ty)

lrt(M3.ty, M3r.ty)

plot(varioGram(M3.ty))
```

Using LRT test, the genotype random term has variability within its levels. 

Note that the variogram now is considered more flat, and therefore a better fit was found. Specially in this case, a water channel ran along the head of each of three rows, creating a potential source of enviromental variation. And the original blocking arrangement was not adequate to isolate this source.

```{r fig.height=6, fig.width=12}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(forcats)
library(patchwork)


predM1.ty = as.data.frame(predict(M1.ty, 'clone')$pvals) %>%
  arrange(predicted.value) %>%
  mutate(clone = fct_inorder(clone))

predM2.ty = as.data.frame(predict(M2.ty, 'clone')$pvals) %>%
  arrange(predicted.value) %>%
  mutate(clone = fct_inorder(clone))

predM3.ty = as.data.frame(predict(M3.ty, 'clone')$pvals) %>%
  arrange(predicted.value) %>%
  mutate(clone = fct_inorder(clone))

se_limits = range(c(predM1.ty$std.error,
                    predM2.ty$std.error,
                    predM3.ty$std.error), na.rm = TRUE)

se_scale = scale_color_viridis_c(limits = se_limits,
                                 name = "Standard Error")

# --- Model 1
se1 = ggplot(predM1.ty,
             aes(y = clone, x = predicted.value, color = std.error)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = predicted.value - std.error,
                    xmax = predicted.value + std.error),
                orientation = "y") +
  se_scale

# --- Model 2
se2 = ggplot(predM2.ty,
             aes(y = clone, x = predicted.value, color = std.error)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = predicted.value - std.error,
                    xmax = predicted.value + std.error),
                orientation = "y") +
  se_scale

# --- Model 3
se3 = ggplot(predM3.ty,
             aes(y = clone, x = predicted.value, color = std.error)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = predicted.value - std.error,
                    xmax = predicted.value + std.error),
                orientation = "y") +
  se_scale

se1 + se2 + se3 +
  plot_layout(guides = 'collect', axes = 'collect')
```

## **AIC, BIC, $H^2$ and ranking**

$$
H^2 = \frac{\sigma_g^2}{\sigma_g^2+\sigma_e^2}
$$

```{r}
ans = data.frame(Trait = rep(c("TY"), each = 3),
                 model = as.factor(paste0("M", 1:3)),
                 AIC, 
                 BIC,
                 varG,
                 varE,
                 H2)

kable(ans, 
      format = "latex", 
      booktabs = TRUE,          
      longtable = TRUE,        
      align = "c") %>%  
  kable_styling(latex_options = c("striped"),
                font_size = 12)
```

This shows that spatial analysis can reveal genotype differences that were masked by environmental heterogeneity in the raw data or simpler models. Because, spatial models can **(i) removel spatial heterogeneity**, **(ii) Improve separation of genetic and environmental effects** and **(iii) the model changes the covariance structure**.

```{r fig.height=5}
# --- TY
pred = bind_rows(
  predM1.ty %>% select(clone, predicted.value) %>% mutate(model ="M1"),
  predM2.ty %>% select(clone, predicted.value) %>% mutate(model ="M2"),
  predM3.ty %>% select(clone, predicted.value) %>% mutate(model = "M3"))

pred = pred %>%
  group_by(model) %>%
  mutate(rank = rank(-predicted.value, ties.method = "average")) %>%
  ungroup()

ggplot(pred,aes(x = model,y = rank, group = clone, color = clone)) +
  geom_line(size = 2) +
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  scale_y_reverse(breaks = 1:12, limits = c(12,1)) +
  labs(x = " ", y = "Rank")+
  theme_minimal()+
  theme(legend.title = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 18),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 14),
        legend.position = 'right',
        legend.text = element_text(size = 14))
```
